guideTitle: 6 Best Headboard Gap Wedge Pillows in 2026
metaDescription: Six headboard gap filler wedge pillows compared by gap range, bed size, foam density and extras, so pillows and phones stop disappearing behind the bed.
introParagraphs: A headboard gap wedge solves a very specific, very annoying problem: the space between mattress and headboard that swallows pillows, phones, glasses and remote controls. A long triangular wedge fills that space, props your pillows at a gentle angle and gives you a firmer backrest when you sit up. It is not a sleep-incline wedge, so the buying rules are different from the rest of this category.

The most important number is the gap range the wedge is designed to fill. In this lineup the Vekkia Headboard Gap Wedge Pillow is rated for 0 to 6 inches, the HOMBYS Foldable Headboard Gap Wedge Pillow and Teemour Headboard Gap Wedge Pillow for 0 to 7, XetraDesign's gap filler for up to 7, and the IFNOW and Homemate gap fillers for 0 to 8. A wedge that is too small slips through the gap, so measuring first matters more than any other step.

These are comfort and bedroom-organizing products, not medical devices. We evaluated them from specifications and buyer feedback, concentrating on gap range, bed size, foam density and the small extras, like pockets, that decide how pleasant they are to live with.

products.name: IFNOW Queen Headboard Gap Wedge Pillow
products.description:
The IFNOW is rated to fill gaps from 0 to 8 inches, the widest range in this comparison along with the Homemate. It measures 60 by 6 by 10 inches in the Queen size, and the listing adds larger, thicker pockets on both sides to increase storage and give the wedge more firmness. That combination suits beds with tall frames or thick mattresses where the gap is bigger than average.

The pockets are the practical bonus. A flat wedge can feel like a block of foam, but pockets turn it into a small shelf that holds a phone, glasses or tablet. Thick pockets also reduce the chance of the wedge flopping over. The foam is described as high-density, which is the right choice for something that must keep its shape.

The tradeoff is that a wedge rated for large gaps may feel bulky on a bed where the gap is small. It also fills the space between the mattress and headboard rather than creating a sleeping incline, so anyone looking for a head-and-torso slope should look elsewhere. For tall beds, it is the strongest choice.
products.bestFor: Tall beds and thick mattresses with big headboard gaps.

products.name: HOMBYS Foldable Headboard Gap Wedge Pillow
products.description:
The HOMBYS stands out because it folds. The listing describes an upgraded folding type that closes gaps from 0 to 7 inches, with triangles on the wedge that let you adjust how much of the space it fills. That is a clever answer to the problem of gaps that vary along the length of a bed, or between old and new mattresses.

It uses 25D high-density memory foam, which the listing says provides superior durability and support. Compared with a flat solid wedge such as the Vekkia Headboard Gap Wedge Pillow, the folding design gives more control but also more places for the foam to shift. It is sold in Queen and King sizes, so check the length against your mattress.

Ownership is easy once set up, though the folding feature adds a small learning curve. It is a good fit if your gap is not a perfect fixed number or if you may change mattresses. For a plain, rigid fill, a solid triangle will be simpler. The folding feature also helps if you move house and the new frame has a different gap. Expect to spend a few minutes adjusting it when you first make the bed.
products.bestFor: Beds whose gap varies or changes over time.
pros: Sold in Queen and King sizes
cons: Fold lines add a small learning curve
More parts to shift than a solid wedge

products.name: Vekkia Headboard Gap Wedge Pillow
products.description:
The Vekkia is a straightforward solid wedge rated for 0 to 6 inches, and its curved top surface is shaped to align with your pillows at a gentle angle. The listing describes the shape as improved through feedback from sleepers, and the high-density foam is intended to provide even, stable support. It is sold in the King size here.

A 0 to 6 inch range is narrower than the IFNOW Queen Headboard Gap Wedge Pillow, so it is best for standard beds rather than tall ones. That narrower range is also an advantage, because a wedge sized to a smaller gap tends to fit snugly and stay put. Simplicity is the appeal: there is nothing to fold, adjust or assemble.

The limit is flexibility. If your gap changes or is larger than 6 inches, the wedge may slide down. It also lacks the pockets that many rivals add. If you want a clean, fuss-free gap filler for a standard-height bed, it is a good choice.
products.bestFor: Standard-height beds that want a clean solid wedge.
pros: Simple solid design, nothing to fold

products.name: Homemate King Headboard Gap Wedge Pillow
products.description:
The Homemate comes in four length sizes to suit a range of beds, and the King pictured here fills gaps from 0 to 8 inches, matching the IFNOW for range. The listing describes a triangle measuring 6.5 by 5 inches, and it is made from 25D high-density foam. Offering a length for most bed sizes means a closer fit than one-size products.

The listing also notes that the wedge can be used with ordinary pillows to elevate your head and neck, so it doubles as a mild backrest. That second use makes it feel more versatile than a plain gap filler. Compared with the HOMBYS Foldable Headboard Gap Wedge Pillow, it is a rigid triangle without folds.

It does not list pockets or a non-slip base. It is a clean, functional choice whose strength is range and size options. If you want a wide gap range without paying for extras, it fits. Because it is a plain triangle, it is easy to wipe down and easy to move. Pair it with a fitted sheet that has some texture so it stays put.
products.bestFor: Buyers who need a specific bed length and a wide gap range.
cons: No pockets or non-slip base listed

products.name: XetraDesign Headboard Gap Wedge Pillow
products.description:
The XetraDesign is the engineering project of the group. Its patent-pending 4-in-1 design allows four different arrangements, and a pressure-locking mechanism is meant to stop it from shifting, unlike traditional triangular pillows that can move around. It also works as an L-shaped triangle, which makes it useful beyond the bed.

The gap range is up to 7 inches, placing it between the Vekkia Headboard Gap Wedge Pillow at 6 and the IFNOW Queen Headboard Gap Wedge Pillow at 8. Because it combines several modes, it asks for a little thought when you first set it up. Once placed, the locking approach aims to keep it stable through restless nights.

The cost of cleverness is complexity. A simple solid triangle has fewer ways to be assembled wrongly. If you have had a plain wedge shift on you before, this is the one to try. Read the setup instructions once so the locking feature does what it should. It is a more involved purchase than the Teemour Headboard Gap Wedge Pillow.
products.bestFor: Restless sleepers whose gap fillers keep shifting.
cons: Patent-pending design is unproven long term

products.name: Teemour Headboard Gap Wedge Pillow
products.description:
The Teemour pairs a 0 to 7 inch gap range with an upgraded non-slip bottom and a removable cover, three details that matter in daily use. The bottom grip keeps the wedge from creeping, the high-density foam resists collapse, and the cover can come off for washing. It is sold as a patented long bed pillow for headboard gaps.

Compared with the Homemate King Headboard Gap Wedge Pillow, the Teemour trades a little range for better stability and easier cleaning. Compared with the XetraDesign Headboard Gap Wedge Pillow, it is simpler and more predictable.

It does not list adjustable folds or pockets, so it is a plain but well-finished wedge. For people who care about cleaning and slip resistance more than extras, it is the most practical. A removable cover also lets you change the look of the bed without replacing the foam. It is a sensible default for a standard-height bed.
products.bestFor: People who want easy cleaning and a grippy base.
pros: Non-slip bottom keeps it in place

buyingCriteria.explanation: The single most important step is measuring the distance between mattress and headboard, then choosing a wedge rated for it. In this lineup the Vekkia covers 0 to 6 inches, the HOMBYS Foldable and Teemour cover 0 to 7, and the IFNOW and Homemate cover 0 to 8. A wedge that is too small slips down, and one that is too big bulges awkwardly. Measure at several points along the bed, since gaps often vary.

These wedges are sold by length. The IFNOW is 60 inches in the Queen size, and the Homemate and Vekkia list King versions. A wedge that is too short leaves the end of the headboard open, and one that is too long is hard to fit. Check your mattress width and choose the matching size.

A gap filler carries your pillows and often your back, so it needs dense foam. The HOMBYS and Homemate both list 25D high-density foam, and the Vekkia and IFNOW list high-density foam. Soft foam will compress and let the wedge slide. A dense triangle holds its shape for years.

Thick mattresses and memory foam toppers can drift away from the headboard, making the gap larger over time. A foldable or adjustable wedge, like the HOMBYS Foldable Headboard Gap Wedge Pillow, copes with that change better than a rigid one. If your bed has a topper, measure with it in place. Check again after a few weeks, since toppers and soft mattresses settle and shift. A wedge rated for a little more than your current gap leaves room for that drift.

Pockets turn a wedge into a bedside shelf, and the IFNOW has larger, thicker ones. A removable cover, as on the Teemour, makes cleaning easier because gaps collect dust. Weigh these extras against simplicity. Thick pockets can add bulk if you overload them, and covers can bunch if they are loose. Choose extras you will use every night, not ones that merely look good on the listing.

A wedge that creeps out of position is frustrating. The Teemour has a non-slip bottom and the XetraDesign has a pressure-locking mechanism. If your previous wedge slipped, prioritize a design that addresses it. Slippage usually comes from slick sheets, a wedge that is too small or foam that is too soft. A grippy bottom solves only one of those, so fit still matters most.

howWeEvaluated.title: Gap range
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the stated gap range of every pick, from the 0 to 6 inch Vekkia Headboard Gap Wedge Pillow to the 0 to 8 inch IFNOW Queen Headboard Gap Wedge Pillow and Homemate King Headboard Gap Wedge Pillow. A wide range helps with taller beds and changing mattresses. We also considered that a wedge rated for a bigger gap than yours can feel bulky. Snug fit counts for more than headline range.

howWeEvaluated.title: Foam and construction
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at stated foam density, such as the 25D foam on the HOMBYS Foldable Headboard Gap Wedge Pillow and Homemate, and at shape details like the Vekkia's curved top. Dense foam resists sagging under pillows and body weight. We treated listings that name a density as more reliable than ones that only say foam.

howWeEvaluated.title: Stability
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered non-slip bases and locking designs. The Teemour Headboard Gap Wedge Pillow and XetraDesign Headboard Gap Wedge Pillow earned credit here. We asked whether a design deals with slipping on slick sheets, which is the commonest complaint. Where a listing said nothing about stability we scored it neutrally.

howWeEvaluated.title: Extras and care
howWeEvaluated.description: Pockets and removable covers were counted as daily conveniences. The IFNOW leads on pockets and the Teemour on cover care.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lineup positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: The IFNOW leads on range and pockets, the HOMBYS on adjustability, the Vekkia on simplicity, the Homemate on length options, the XetraDesign on locking and the Teemour on grip and cleaning. This is based on specifications and buyer feedback.

faq.q: How do I know what size headboard gap wedge to buy?
faq.a: Measure the gap between mattress and headboard at a few points, then choose a wedge rated for at least that distance. The Vekkia is rated for 0 to 6 inches and the IFNOW for 0 to 8. Also match the length to your mattress width.

faq.q: Why does my gap filler keep slipping down?
faq.a: It is probably too small for the gap, or the foam is too soft. Choose a wedge rated for your gap and made from dense foam. A non-slip base, like the Teemour's, also helps.

faq.q: Can I sleep on a headboard gap wedge?
faq.a: They are designed to fill a gap and prop pillows, not to be a sleeping incline. Some can act as a mild backrest. If you want a sleeping slope, choose a regular bed wedge.

faq.q: Does a thick mattress change the gap?
faq.a: Yes. A thick mattress or a topper can sit further from the headboard, widening the gap. Measure with everything on the bed. A foldable wedge handles change better.
If you keep a phone, glasses or remote in bed, they are very handy. The IFNOW has larger, thicker pockets. If you prefer a clean look, skip them.

faq.q: How do I clean a gap wedge?
faq.a: Remove the cover if there is one, as on the Teemour, and wash it according to the label. Vacuum the gap itself. Dust collects in these gaps, so a filler that seals it helps.

faq.q: Will a gap wedge damage my headboard?
faq.a: A foam wedge is soft and unlikely to scratch. Still, check that it sits flat and does not press hard on delicate trim. A snug fit is better than a forced one.
